Retraining the classifier with validated clips

Source: vignettes/retraining.Rmd
retraining.Rmd

The manual review of stage 1 produces two kinds of labelled clips: clips that contain the species (positives) and clips in which the classifier detected the species but the reviewer did not hear it (negatives). Besides measuring precision and feeding the calibration, both can be used to retrain the BirdNET custom classifier. This article shows how to turn the reviewed clips into a training data set in the layout that BirdNET-Analyzer expects, how to keep an independent set for testing the new classifier, and what has to be redone after retraining.

Training itself runs in BirdNET-Analyzer (Python), not in R. The requirements quoted below come from the BirdNET-Analyzer documentation (version 2.4.0, section birdnet_analyzer.train of the command line interface); check the version you use, since the training options change between releases.

library(sheepdog)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
ex <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")

What BirdNET-Analyzer expects

According to its documentation, the training script of BirdNET-Analyzer:

  • takes a folder with one subfolder per class, and uses the folder names as labels. The recommended label format is <scientific name>_<common name>, although other formats work;
  • accepts negative samples of a class in a folder with the same name prefixed by - (e.g. -Boana raniceps_boa-ran). Negative samples are used for training only, not for validation, and only when the folder with the positives of that class exists;
  • treats a folder named Noise, Background, Other or Silence as a non-event class;
  • resamples the audio to 48 kHz and works on 3 s segments;
  • recommends at least 100 audio files per species, although training also works with fewer;
  • accepts an independent test set (--test_data).

The documentation also states that custom classifiers trained with BirdNET-Analyzer are licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

The clips cut by sheepdog already fit this layout: they are 3 s segments of the original recordings, and species_code keeps the full label of the classifier (<scientific name>_<code>), which can be used as the folder name so that the retrained classifier reports the same labels.

The reviewed clips

We use the reviewed clips shipped with the package. In a real project the review is done in the Review tab of the BirdNET GUI, which moves each clip into a Positive or Negative subfolder; here we recreate that folder structure with empty .wav files from the verdicts of the example tables, and read it back with classify_review(), which records where each clip was found (reviewed_path).

validation <- read_validation_tables(
  list.files(file.path(ex, "validation"), full.names = TRUE))

review_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "review")
unlink(review_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dest <- file.path(review_dir, validation$species_folder,
                  ifelse(validation$verdict == "positive",
                         "Positive", "Negative"))
for (d in unique(dest)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
invisible(file.create(file.path(dest, validation$clip_file)))

reviewed <- validation |>
  select(-verdict, -reviewed_path) |>
  classify_review(review_dir) |>
  suppressMessages()
count(reviewed, species_code, verdict)
#> # A tibble: 16 × 3
#>    species_code                      verdict      n
#>    <chr>                             <chr>    <int>
#>  1 Boana raniceps_boa-ran            negative    88
#>  2 Boana raniceps_boa-ran            positive   232
#>  3 Dendropsophus nanus_den-nan       negative   161
#>  4 Dendropsophus nanus_den-nan       positive   159
#>  5 Elachistocleis bicolor_ela-bic    negative    34
#>  6 Elachistocleis bicolor_ela-bic    positive   286
#>  7 Leptodactylus fuscus_lep-fus      negative   151
#>  8 Leptodactylus fuscus_lep-fus      positive    98
#>  9 Leptodactylus podicipinus_lep-pod negative    43
#> 10 Leptodactylus podicipinus_lep-pod positive   255
#> 11 Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv       negative    32
#> 12 Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv       positive   288
#> 13 Pseudis platensis_pse-pla         negative   220
#> 14 Pseudis platensis_pse-pla         positive   100
#> 15 Scinax nasicus_sci-nas            negative   161
#> 16 Scinax nasicus_sci-nas            positive   159

read_validation_tables() stacks the validation_by_clip.csv tables of several sites or rounds, keeping every column and verdict.

Keeping an independent test set

A retrained classifier has to be evaluated on clips that it did not see during training. BirdNET-Analyzer holds out a validation split (--val_split) drawn from the training folder itself, but clips from the same site and night share background noise and calling individuals, so a random split of clips tends to overstate performance (our recommendation, not a statement of the BirdNET documentation). A stricter test keeps whole sites out of training and passes them as --test_data. Here we hold out one site.

Building the training folders

build_training_set() copies the reviewed clips into the BirdNET layout: positives in <set>/<species_code>/ and negatives in <set>/-<species_code>/, where <set> is train, or test for the sites in test_sites. It reads each clip from reviewed_path, the place where the review left it, leaves out whole-recording clips (which have no confidence score), writes the table of copied clips to training_set.csv, and warns about classes with fewer positive training files than min_files (100 by default, the number recommended by the BirdNET documentation).

training_root <- file.path(tempdir(), "birdnet_training")
unlink(training_root, recursive = TRUE)
training_set <- build_training_set(reviewed, training_root,
                                   test_sites = "NHE") |>
  suppressMessages()
#> Warning: Class(es) with fewer than 100 positive training files: Leptodactylus
#> fuscus_lep-fus (48), Pseudis platensis_pse-pla (76)

list.files(file.path(training_root, "train"))
#>  [1] "-Boana raniceps_boa-ran"            "-Dendropsophus nanus_den-nan"      
#>  [3] "-Elachistocleis bicolor_ela-bic"    "-Leptodactylus fuscus_lep-fus"     
#>  [5] "-Leptodactylus podicipinus_lep-pod" "-Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv"      
#>  [7] "-Pseudis platensis_pse-pla"         "-Scinax nasicus_sci-nas"           
#>  [9] "Boana raniceps_boa-ran"             "Dendropsophus nanus_den-nan"       
#> [11] "Elachistocleis bicolor_ela-bic"     "Leptodactylus fuscus_lep-fus"      
#> [13] "Leptodactylus podicipinus_lep-pod"  "Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv"       
#> [15] "Pseudis platensis_pse-pla"          "Scinax nasicus_sci-nas"
count(training_set, set, verdict)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 3
#>   set   verdict      n
#>   <chr> <chr>    <int>
#> 1 test  negative   275
#> 2 test  positive   365
#> 3 train negative   615
#> 4 train positive  1212

How many positive training files each class received:

n_pos <- training_set |>
  filter(set == "train", verdict == "positive") |>
  count(species_code) |>
  mutate(below_100 = n < 100)
n_pos
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   species_code                          n below_100
#>   <chr>                             <int> <lgl>    
#> 1 Boana raniceps_boa-ran              197 FALSE    
#> 2 Dendropsophus nanus_den-nan         118 FALSE    
#> 3 Elachistocleis bicolor_ela-bic      222 FALSE    
#> 4 Leptodactylus fuscus_lep-fus         48 TRUE     
#> 5 Leptodactylus podicipinus_lep-pod   194 FALSE    
#> 6 Physalaemus cuvieri_phy-cuv         217 FALSE    
#> 7 Pseudis platensis_pse-pla            76 TRUE     
#> 8 Scinax nasicus_sci-nas              140 FALSE

With the 2467 reviewed clips of the example, 2 of the 8 classes have fewer than 100 positive training files. Classes with few positives are the ones that most need clips from further review rounds before retraining.

Which clips to add

Three points about the composition of the training set follow from how the clips were chosen (our recommendations, not statements of the BirdNET documentation):

  • Clips from the "top" design are the easy cases. They are the highest-scoring detections, so they teach the classifier little about the calls it currently misses or scores low. Positives from the "random_detections" and "random_recordings" designs (see vignette("sampling-designs")) cover lower scores and calls the classifier did not detect.
  • Negatives with high scores are the most informative. They are the sounds the classifier confuses with the species. Species with many high-scoring false positives in precision_by_bin() (see vignette("validation-effort")) are the ones for which negatives matter most.
  • Whole-recording clips of "random_recordings" are longer than 3 s. BirdNET-Analyzer crops long files (--crop_mode), but the label of a whole recording says only that the species was heard somewhere in it. Cut the annotated calls into 3 s clips before using them as positives.

Training

Training runs in a Python environment with BirdNET-Analyzer installed. The commands below follow the example of the documentation (they are not run here):

python -m birdnet_analyzer.train birdnet_training/train \
  --test_data birdnet_training/test \
  -o checkpoints/custom/Custom_Classifier.tflite

python -m birdnet_analyzer.analyze recordings/ \
  --classifier checkpoints/custom/Custom_Classifier.tflite

Use --model_format raven (or both) if the classifier will also be used in Raven. Hyperparameters such as --hidden_units, --learning_rate, --dropout and the upsampling options affect the result; the documentation recommends trying several settings, or --autotune.

After retraining

A retrained classifier produces new confidence scores, so everything that was estimated from the scores of the old one no longer applies:

  1. Run the new classifier over the recordings to obtain new selection tables.
  2. Draw and review a new set of clips (stage 1). Do not reuse the clips used for training: their scores are biased upwards on the data the classifier was trained on.
  3. Recalibrate (stage 2, vignette("calibration")) and rebuild the detection histories and community matrices (stage 3).

Keep training_set.csv with the new classifier. Before reviewing the detections of the retrained classifier, exclude_training_clips() drops from the new manifest the clips that overlap, for the same species and recording, a clip used in training:

manifest_v2 <- select_clips(detections_v2, ...) |>
  exclude_training_clips(file.path(training_root, "training_set.csv"))

extract_validation_clips() records the classifier label in extraction_info.csv, so each validation round can be traced to the classifier that produced its clips.
